guards.what: G2 (LIVE): Hook.ModifyGeneratedMapLate has exactly ONE caller in the game -- the save-load branch of RunManager.GenerateMap -- and the sim runs it on every fresh map generation
guards.issue: Closed 2026-07-29 (round 7): Fur Coat no longer OVERRIDES the Late map hook. `grep -rn ModifyGeneratedMapLate src/` outside AbstractModel.cs/Hook.cs returns three lines: the two implementers (SpoilsMap.cs:63, FurCoat.cs:58) and ONE dispatch, at RunManager.cs:740 -- inside `if (SavedMapsToLoad != null && SavedMapsToLoad.TryGetValue(...))`, the branch that DESERIALIZES a saved ActMap (re-read today at RunManager.cs:732-742). The branch that GENERATES a map (:743-747) runs ModifyGeneratedMap and AfterMapGenerated ONLY; the Late hook exists to re-attach quests/shape to a loaded map, and the sim has no save-load. So relics/fur_coat.py's override is GONE, with the enumeration written where it used to be, and the marks are now set exactly once -- by `after_obtained`. WHAT WAS TRIED FIRST AND BACKED OUT, because it belongs to another record: removing the sim's Late PASS from `RunState._generate_map` altogether. That is what the source says for Fur Coat, but it broke three card/spoils_map tests -- SpoilsMap overrides BOTH map hooks (SpoilsMap.cs:49 replaces the map, :63 records the Treasure coord that its AfterMapGenerated then pins its quest to), so on the sim's only path the card needs the Late pass to do anything. Reconciling THAT with a hook the game only dispatches on load is the CARD stream's entry, not this relic's, so the pass is kept with the mismatch documented in `_generate_map`, and Fur Coat is fixed by not implementing the hook. Both consequences this entry recorded are closed either way: the sim no longer re-marks or RE-ROLLS Fur Coat's coords when Golden Compass regenerates the same act's map (it rolled five fresh coords off a new event-rng shuffle where the game leaves the persisted FurCoatCoordCols/Rows untouched), and it no longer burns a Fur Coat shuffle the game never takes. EXECUTED: `modify_generated_map_late` is absent from `FurCoat.__dict__`, the inherited base no-op returns the map unchanged, and a call to it leaves `marked_coords` byte-identical. Pinned by test/test_relic_live_tail.py's two fur_coat map tests. NOT CLOSED: SpoilsMap's own exposure to the same dispatcher, which is the card stream's. The else branch that GENERATES a map (RunManager.cs:745-747) runs ModifyGeneratedMap and AfterMapGenerated and NOT the Late pass. MECHANISM: CreatureCmd.SetCurrentHp (CreatureCmd.cs:762-779) does three things the raw assignment does not -- it fires `Hook.AfterCurrentHpChanged(runState, combatState, creature, delta)` whenever the value actually changed, it plays a revive animation when a dead creature is raised above 0, and it calls Kill(creature) if the new value leaves the creature dead. The sim HAS the notification hook (`on_hp_changed`, hooks.py:506-510) and fur_coat.py does not call it. DORMANT: the sim's only on_hp_changed implementer is relics/red_skull.py:45, which reads the PLAYER's HP, and Fur Coat only ever touches enemies; the C# implementers that would care are monster models (Crusher and Rocket both override AfterCurrentHpChanged, and Crusher's pairs it with BeforeDeath), and audit/records/seam/hook_dispatch.json gap G5 already records that MonsterModel is not a sim hook listener at all -- so there is no sim listener to notify even if the call were added. The Kill branch cannot fire here (the target value is 1, and the relic runs before any enemy is dead). Porting a player-side or power-side on_hp_changed listener that reads enemy HP, or making monsters listeners (hook_dispatch G5's fix), makes it live. The comment at fur_coat.py:83 ('SetCurrentHp: a raw set, no damage pipeline') is correct about the damage pipeline and silent about the notification.

guards.what: N2: the marking RNG -- `new Rng(base.Owner, base.Id)` then `UnstableShuffle` (FurCoat.cs:77, 83) vs `make_event_rng(run.rng_set.seed, self.id.upper()).shuffle(candidates)` (fur_coat.py:41-45)
guards.rationale: Rng(Player, ModelId, mixin=0, counter=0) seeds from `RunState.Rng.Seed + GetPlayerSlotIndex(player) + GetDeterministicHashCode(id.Entry)` (Rng.cs:47-50); in single player the slot index is 0, so it reduces to run seed + hash(Entry), which is exactly make_event_rng (rng.py:70-82). The Entry for FurCoat slugifies to 'FUR_COAT', which is `self.id.upper()`. Rng.shuffle (rng.py:270-273) is the same descending Fisher-Yates as ListExtensions.UnstableShuffle (ListExtensions.cs:45-60), drawing NextInt(i+1) per step. Note this is a per-relic stream that is NOT re-mixed, so a second marking in the same run repeats the same shuffle on both sides -- which is why G2's extra sim re-mark is a wrong-marks bug rather than a fresh-random one.

guards.what: N3: the candidate set and its ORDER -- `map.GetAllMapPoints().Where(p => (uint)(p.PointType - 5) <= 1u && !p.Quests.Any(q => q is FurCoat))` (FurCoat.cs:78-82) vs `[p for p in act_map.all_points() if p.point_type in (MONSTER, ELITE)]` (fur_coat.py:33-36)
guards.rationale: UnstableShuffle is order-dependent by construction (its own doc comment says so), so the enumeration order is load-bearing. ActMap.GetAllMapPoints iterates column-major, `for c in columns: for r in rows`, skipping nulls (ActMap.cs:34-47); actmap.py:388-394's all_points is the identical loop, and its docstring cites the source. MapPointType is Unassigned=0, Unknown=1, Shop=2, Treasure=3, RestSite=4, Monster=5, Elite=6, Boss=7, Ancient=8, so `(uint)(pointType - 5) <= 1u` is exactly {Monster, Elite}. The dropped `!p.Quests.Any(q => q is FurCoat)` clause is a no-op on the marking path: it only matters when re-marking a map that already carries this relic's quests, and the sim replaces marked_coords wholesale instead of accumulating (fur_coat.py:46-48), reaching the same set. Both sides Take(7) from the shuffled list (`Combats` = DynamicVar 7m, FurCoat.cs:49, no AscensionHelper branch; COMBATS = 7, fur_coat.py:18).
